speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Police officers from the Public Transport Security Command (TransCom), a specialist unit within the SPF commissioned in 2009, conduct patrols within the public transport network to project police presence.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This helps to deter and detect crime, including cases of outrage of modesty.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Police have also been active in their crime prevention outreach to commuters.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Police display posters on trains and train station platforms, screen videos and conduct crime prevention roadshows in train stations and bus interchanges to raise commuters' vigilance against crime, including outrage of modesty.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Commuters are reminded to be aware of their surroundings, look out for suspicious persons and to take steps to protect themselves from being victims of crime.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Courts have been meting out stiff sentences for those convicted of molestation on trains.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Though it is only 5%, I believe there are a lot of cases not reported because the victims feel very embarrassed.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, I would like to ask the Parliamentary Secretary whether the Ministry will step up education, that means to educate commuters, remind them about personal space, educate victims how to make reports and what are the key details that need to be furnished.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The next question is whether there are sufficient cameras on the train platforms or inside the carriages to help to deter crimes.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: As for the suggestion to step up awareness, there has been cooperation with the public transport operators, and these have included in-train panels, advertisements and videos to encourage people to be aware to protect themselves.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: As for the adequacy of cameras in trains, for operational reasons, I am not able to go into detail on the use of cameras on the trains, but the Member can be assured that this is something that we take very seriously, and not just for outrage of modesty case but the general security of our trains.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I do not think we have reached that stage.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: As the Member has heard, the number of cases is very small, it is 5%; I do not think we would go to such a drastic measure at this stage.
